Q: How do I handle read system calls for HPC? A:

It kinda doesn't matter how one goes about reading data; most modern OSes do a pretty good job at caching / optimising file I/O so that you don't have to. There's minor savings in time by cutting down the number of system calls.

Understanding where the processing power is being used is key. You're reading CSV files? Well, a lot of compute is going to be spent on converting the text in the csv files into data values (floats? ints?) in your program. Text to int conversion will take several clock cycles, and many accesses to cached memory with a strong possibility of cache misses and the slowness related to those. If the data is floating point "0.314159256E+1" format, there's a fair bit of branching in that too; there has to be checks for all the non-numerical characters.

Whereas adding up a whole bunch of ints can (with a good compiler that understands AVX or similar) take just one clock cycle.

Parsing text from a csv file can be partially parallelised. Reading rows cannot be parallelised; one has to read every single byte of the file one by one to identify rows. Even if you've not written it like that in your code, functions that read whole lines on your behalf have to do that. If one has read several rows, those can be processed in parallel, but a row itself cannot be processed in parallel; one still has to process the row byte by byte looking for the commas. All in all, CSV is not a good file format for the movement of a large volume of data. The same applies to any text representation (like JSON or XML).

The same will go for data output. If your results are in CSV format, there's a good chance that the creation of that text is more burdensome than the maths done.

Q: Creating table to specify compression option A: 
<table_option> ::=  
{  
    [DATA_COMPRESSION = { NONE | ROW | PAGE }  
      [ ON PARTITIONS ( { <partition_number_expression> | <range> }   
      [ , ...n ] ) ]]  

.....

Would you please enlist all possible ways to format this with data compression option ?

values in square brackets are mandatory..so below are mandatory

data_Compression,ON PARTITIONS,..n

values in flower brackets means you will need to select one of them.

In this case

{ NONE | ROW | PAGE }

can be read as None or Row or Page..

so finally

data_Compression = none or row or page on partitions(1) or partitions (1-2)

Q: access multiple camera via RTSP and display them on WEB? A:

There has media source extensions(MSE) can support live h264 with very low latency(Chrome Firefox Safari below 1s). but there need a gateway to convert RTSP to fragmented MP4. https://github.com/linkingvision/h5stream this link may help you test the performance of the MSE latency. and you can test the multi RTSP source.
